To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the performance of the texture methods varies considerably depending on the type of texture and the type of texture analysis, (2) the texture spectrum is the best method for the MeasTex database, (3) the texture spectrum combined with feature selection is the best method on the VisTex database, and (4) texture methods are not as effective for the Meas Tex database as for the VisTex database
the best results are obtained using a feature selection algorithm applied to a combination of texture operators and Law's masks.
the best performance is obtained with the texture spectrum, followed by the binary stack method, the co-occurrence matrix, the edge frequency, and Law's masks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (1) to evaluate and compare the relative performance of texture methods on two standard texture benchmarks (VisTex and MeasTex), (2) to investigate feature selection techniques to improve recognition performance, (3) to compare different texture features for their ability to classify texture images, (4) to compare the relative performance between the two texture benchmarks.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best results are obtained by a combination of methods.
the best results were obtained by the texture operators (TO) and the texture spectrum (TS).
the texture spectrum is superior for texture recognition, and that the edge frequency is the best of the traditional methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
texture operators are the most effective, followed by Law's masks, and the binary stack method.
the texture analysis methods considered in this paper are not very effective for texture recognition, but they can be very useful for texture classification.
, while there is a large number of texture analysis methods available, they are all limited in their ability to discriminate texture patterns.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the texture descriptors is not very different.
the texture operators and the texture spectrum are the best performing texture features for the two databases.
the texture analysis problem is far from being solved, and that the use of a single technique, or even multiple techniques, is insufficient to obtain a satisfactory recognition performance.
